title: Quick check: CSS-in-JS

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “CSS-in-JS”?
options: The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
The concept of styling through JavaScript is best handled through explicit, read-only inputs and clear component composition.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
questions.answer_key: The concept of styling through JavaScript is best handled through explicit, read-only inputs and clear component composition.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in CSS-in-JS: The concept of styling through JavaScript is best handled through explicit, read-only inputs and clear component composition.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying The concept of styling through JavaScript?
options: Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Keep props immutable and move shared state to the nearest common owner.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
questions.answer_key: Keep props immutable and move shared state to the nearest common owner.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in CSS-in-JS: Keep props immutable and move shared state to the nearest common owner.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “CSS-in-JS” complete?
options: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in CSS-in-JS: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
